animations.title: Document processing: intake to outcome
animations.subtitle: One PDF moves through acceptance, a durable queue and configured execution
animations.legend: Follow the teal connectors. Job status and document status are separate records.

db.title: SQLite acceptance
db.detail: Batch, document, source file and job

worker.title: One local worker
worker.detail: Claims a queued job with a lease

stages.title: Choose a version before accepting work
stages.text: A web upload selects an eligible published version. A watch-folder claim uses its current binding's exact version. Input validation happens before accepted work is queued.
stages.note: Invalid or stale assignments do not create accepted work.

stages.title: Persist acceptance and the processing job
stages.text: Ingestion records the batch, document, source artifact reference and processing job together. The PDF bytes live on disk; SQLite retains the pinned assignment and durable work record.
stages.note: Filesystem moves are outside SQLite atomicity and need compensation.

stages.title: Claim the job, then start the document
stages.text: The worker leases one queued job and sets the document to processing. Job queued/running and document progress belong to different lifecycles; neither should be inferred from a UI label.
stages.note: A workflow may finish its job while its document awaits review.

stages.title: Execute the immutable configured pipeline
stages.text: WorkflowLoader approves task implementations, starts attributed task runs and executes the pinned task order. Tasks persist extraction results and register durable output files as they run.
stages.note: Stop/continue policy records failures; continued errors remain visible.

stages.title: Finalize work without hiding a review pause
stages.text: Ordinary completion or failure runs internal cleanup and leaf finalization. Review pause and split fan-out return before that cleanup path. Aggregate state comes from document leaves, not the job label.
stages.note: Review continuations and split children finish their own configured work.

stages.title: An upload retry can return the same batch
stages.text: With an Idempotency-Key, the same user, pipeline and file fingerprint identifies the original submission. Repeating it returns the accepted batch; changed contents conflict. Clients without a key remain non-idempotent.
stages.note: An unknown receipt does not prove the original request was cancelled.

animations.title: Human review: persisted pause, new flow
animations.subtitle: Extraction review preserves state in SQLite and resumes downstream once
animations.legend: The original flow returns. Human review is not a suspended Prefect execution.

review.title: SQLite review item
review.detail: Pinned form and paused task run

downstream.title: New downstream flow
downstream.detail: Next task, then cleanup and fan-in

stages.title: Evaluate persisted extraction results
stages.text: The review gate evaluates configured policy, required fields, confidence and structured review flags. When review is needed, it creates a review item linked to the document and exact published form.
stages.note: Later form publication does not change this review item's schema.

stages.title: Persist the pause and return from the flow
stages.text: The document becomes review_required and the gate's task run becomes paused. WorkflowLoader returns before downstream tasks and cleanup. SQLite holds the business state while the operator works.
stages.note: The original flow has returned; it is not kept waiting in memory.

stages.title: Claim a time-limited review lock
stages.text: ReviewService claims the item atomically and changes the document to in_review. An active competing lock blocks edits; the current owner can renew it, and an expired lock can be reclaimed.
stages.note: Draft saves and completion require the active lock owner.

stages.title: Validate corrections and commit final values
stages.text: Completion validates corrections against the exact stored form, persists final field values, completes the paused task run and marks the document review_completed. Resume then becomes eligible.
stages.note: Invalid corrections cannot advance the document to resume.

stages.title: Acquire resume once and reconstruct context
stages.text: ResumeManager reloads the pinned pipeline, restores final values and atomically claims review_completed to resuming. It checks existing downstream execution so overlapping requests cannot start the same continuation twice.
stages.note: Only one caller acquires the downstream resume transition.

stages.title: Start a new flow after the review gate
stages.text: A new flow starts at the next configured task, even if only terminal cleanup remains. It uses the document's pinned version. Manual split is different: its continuation re-enters the split task to apply the decision.
stages.note: Manual approval and background dispatch have separate recovery limits.

animations.title: Immutable versions: publish, pin, preserve
animations.subtitle: Existing work keeps its execution contract while future intake can change
animations.legend: Version 1 and version 2 are synthetic examples of exact stored version identities.

old.title: Existing document
old.detail: Pinned: pipeline v1 and form A

stages.title: Validate the draft and its exact dependencies
stages.text: Publication validates task definitions, approvals, secret references and exact review-form dependencies. It rechecks the draft revision under a write transaction before creating an immutable published version.
stages.note: Validation and revision conflicts prevent publication.

stages.title: Pin accepted work to version 1
stages.text: Intake selects an eligible exact version before acceptance. The batch and its documents retain matching pipeline identities; review items later retain the exact form version required by that pipeline.
stages.note: No implicit latest-version substitution during execution.

stages.title: Publish version 2 without rewriting version 1
stages.text: An edited draft publishes a new immutable version and dependency set. Version 1 remains available for already-pinned work. The connector represents version history, not a mutation of version 1.
stages.note: Publication alone does not upgrade existing assignments.

stages.title: Assign version 2 explicitly to future intake
stages.text: An upload can select version 2, or an administrator can change a watch-folder binding. Future accepted documents use that selection. Claims already started keep their recorded assignment.
stages.note: Existing documents still execute pipeline v1 and form A.

new.detail: Pinned: pipeline v2 and form B

stages.title: Load the recorded version again for resume
stages.text: PipelineDefinitionService verifies document and batch assignment, version hashes, approved tasks and exact stored forms. Review resume and split children keep those identities even if the template is later inactive or archived.
stages.note: Missing, mismatched or invalid definitions stop execution.

old.detail: Resume: still pipeline v1 / form A

stages.title: Resolve secrets in memory; restart for YAML edits
stages.text: Stored definitions retain secret aliases, which execution resolves in memory from deployment configuration. Each process owns its YAML snapshot, so deployment edits need coordinated restart. SQLite settings and publication have separate semantics.
stages.note: Secrets stay outside published definitions and diagram examples.

v2.detail: Stored aliases; resolved only in memory

animations.title: PDF splitting: fan-out and leaf-derived fan-in
animations.subtitle: Children run sequentially; aggregate state follows leaf outcomes
animations.legend: The three children are synthetic examples. Parent containers are not counted as leaves.

stages.title: Check whether splitting is needed at all
stages.text: One validated segment covering every source page once in original order keeps the original document, file and pinned version. It records single_document and continues downstream without fan-out. Other segment shapes create children.
stages.note: Full ordered coverage keeps the original document identity.

stages.title: Materialize children and record their identities
stages.text: For fan-out, the split materializer creates child PDFs, document relationships, metadata and split_pdf registrations. Children inherit the pinned pipeline. The parent signals fan_out and returns before its normal cleanup path.
stages.note: Partial children require compensation before execution proceeds.

stages.title: Execute downstream work for child A first
stages.text: WorkflowManager loads the children's pinned pipeline and starts each child after the split step, sequentially. Child A completes while other leaves are unfinished, so the root and batch remain processing.
stages.note: Fan-out does not imply a parallel worker pool.

stages.title: A review leaf changes the aggregate
stages.text: Child B pauses for review and its flow returns. Child C can then run and fail. Any review leaf makes the aggregate review_required; the container's own split status does not override that result.
stages.note: A pending human decision prevents a terminal aggregate.

stages.title: Resolve review, then recompute from terminal leaves
stages.text: After child B's review continuation succeeds, the leaves are two completed and one failed. FanInService produces completed_with_errors. All succeeded would yield completed; all failed would yield failed.
stages.note: Only leaves contribute to root and batch outcome counts.

stages.title: Compensate a partially materialized split
stages.text: If a later segment fails during creation, the materializer removes earlier partial children and files. If compensation cannot remove them, remaining partial records are marked failed so source and batch can reach a terminal outcome.
stages.note: This scene precedes child execution; it is not a later retry.

animations.title: Runtime: startup, supervision and recovery
animations.subtitle: A parent process supervises web and worker children sharing SQLite and disk
animations.legend: Normal topology: one migration owner, one web process, one local processing worker.

worker.title: Worker subprocess
worker.detail: Lease jobs and execute root workflows

db.title: SQLite + filesystem
db.detail: Durable jobs, state and PDF contents

stages.title: Initialize the database in the parent
stages.text: main.py resolves deployment configuration and runs startup migration before launching child processes. In the normal supervised topology, the parent alone owns database migration.
stages.note: Migration or validation failure prevents a ready runtime.

stages.title: Launch children in read-only verification mode
stages.text: The parent launches web and worker children. Both verify the exact supported schema and essential tables before accepting work. They share database and filesystem access, while retaining separate process responsibilities.
stages.note: Children do not repair or migrate a mismatched database.

stages.title: Require readiness for this launch's run ID
stages.text: Supervisor, web, worker and watch coordinator must report ready inside a bounded startup window. Worker heartbeat reporting runs independently of OCR, so long provider calls do not silence its heartbeat thread.
stages.note: A bad watch binding can degrade ingestion without losing worker readiness.

health.detail: Fresh run ID; expected components ready

stages.title: Accept durably; execute only in the worker
stages.text: The watch coordinator and web upload path persist accepted jobs. The local worker claims them and executes queued root workflows. Producers acknowledge accepted work independently of its eventual processing outcome.
stages.note: One worker; no distributed queue or multi-host coordination.

stages.title: An unexpected child exit stops the runtime
stages.text: If the worker or web child exits unexpectedly, supervision fails and stops the remaining process trees. Windows shutdown first requests an orderly stop, then forces termination if the grace period expires.
stages.note: The supervisor exits nonzero; recovery needs a later runtime launch.

web.detail: Orderly stop, then forced if needed

health.detail: This run is no longer ready

stages.title: After restart, recover expired job leases
stages.text: A later worker poll returns expired running leases to queued, then can claim available work. SQLite preserves queue records across process interruption, but does not make external side effects transactional. Queue failure retries have separate limits.
stages.note: An interrupted task may need idempotency or operator recovery.

stages.title: Keep queue retry distinct from task retry
stages.text: The worker retries selected startup and input I/O failures within its attempt limit. A flow returning failure or an unclassified exception is terminal at the queue level. Configured task retries are a separate mechanism.
stages.note: Durable acceptance does not imply exactly-once provider execution.

animations.title: Artifacts: file contents and SQLite identity
animations.subtitle: Durable PDFs and exports remain on disk; records explain ownership and access
animations.legend: File creation and database registration are separate operations, with explicit failure limits.

stages.title: Keep source bytes separate from operational records
stages.text: Ingestion stores the original PDF on disk and registers its source_original role for the document. SQLite records identity and location; it does not contain the PDF bytes. Source artifacts have no producer task key.
stages.note: Recovering a database alone does not restore artifact contents.

stages.title: Reserve an output path before writing
stages.text: Built-in split, archive and export operations reserve generated paths with exclusive creation. They write large output contents to the filesystem, keeping concurrent local workflows from selecting the same output path.
stages.note: File creation is not an atomic database transaction.

stages.title: Register artifact identity and producer attribution
stages.text: Tasks call register_document_artifact when a document identity is available. The record stores role, resolved path and metadata; producer attribution uses the configured task_key. Existing matching registrations are reused.
stages.note: split_pdf, source_archive and export_pdf/csv/json identify purpose.

stages.title: Resolve a PDF through its document record
stages.text: The preview endpoint authenticates the user, reads document file candidates and serves only a safe PDF within configured roots. Registered paths support traceability; this endpoint does not filter documents by owner.
stages.note: Authentication and safe paths do not create per-user document isolation.

stages.title: Preserve registered artifacts during housekeeping
stages.text: Task cleanup checks document_files before unlinking a workflow path. Registered artifacts survive this cleanup; transient files can be removed. Processing-history deletion is a different operation and retains physical files.
stages.note: Task housekeeping is not a general artifact retention policy.

stages.title: Account for registration failure explicitly
stages.text: The default helper is best-effort: a registration error warns without replacing the successful file-operation result. A caller-supplied connection selects strict registration in its transaction. Best-effort failure can leave a file without traceability.
stages.note: Disk success alone does not prove the artifact is registered.

animations.title: History cleanup: preview, verify, delete
animations.subtitle: Administrative retention removes eligible records while preserving files and audit history
animations.legend: Synthetic records illustrate the transaction boundary; this animation deletes no real data.

confirm.title: Confirm + revalidate
confirm.detail: Name, actor, expiry and fresh digest

delete.title: One write transaction
delete.detail: Delete selected history and audit it

stages.title: Select whole batches that are safe to remove
stages.text: The cleanup plan excludes active work, pending reviews, live locks, recent activity and inconsistent history. It checks jobs, task runs, decisions and document relationships against an exclusive UTC cutoff.
stages.note: Mixed assignments and cross-batch children are excluded.

stages.title: Bind the preview to an actor and exact data
stages.text: Preview stores a SHA-256 fingerprint of the selected records and plan, with the requesting actor and a 15-minute expiry. It returns counts and exclusions without deleting processing history.
stages.note: Counts describe eligible data at this point in time.

stages.title: Recompute the plan under a write lock
stages.text: Confirmation checks preview identity, actor, expiry and pipeline name. Under BEGIN IMMEDIATE it rebuilds the plan and compares its fingerprint. Changed data or an expired preview requires a fresh preview.
stages.note: A stale digest cannot authorize a different record selection.

stages.title: Delete history and write its audit atomically
stages.text: Dependency-ordered record deletion, receipt trimming, preview consumption and the admin audit event commit together. Artifact registrations are removed with selected history. A retained foreign-key reference aborts and rolls back the transaction.
stages.note: Partial database deletion must not be committed.

stages.title: Keep receipt identities after payload trimming
stages.text: Upload receipts become minimal tombstones while user, key and fingerprint identities remain. Lookup reports purged, preventing a delayed retry of the old accepted submission from recreating deleted processing work.
stages.note: A new upload requires an explicit new submission.

stages.title: Retain the files and historical governance record
stages.text: Cleanup leaves physical PDFs and exports, audit history and immutable version definitions intact. It removes their selected operational registrations. Freed SQLite pages can be reused; this workflow does not run VACUUM or delete files.
stages.note: Database cleanup is separate from filesystem retention and compaction.

retained.detail: Files, audits and versions still exist
